title: introduce-lease-aware-gpu-lifecycle-and-network-segmentation-modules
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: Private installs frequently hit contention on GPU nodepools when multiple tenants request capacity simultaneously and when tfstate boundaries are too coarse for safe incremental upgrades. This PR introduces two complementary Terraform modules plus orchestration helpers: a lease-aware GPU lifecycle module that manages tenant-scoped ephemeral leases (allocation, drain, reprovision) and a network segmentation module that creates per-tenant subnet slices and route policies with deterministic allocation. Design highlights: the GPU lease module exposes a lightweight lease resource, associated IAM roles for ephemeral node provisioning, and a small lifecycle controller hook (stateless) that coordinates lease handoff via a shared tfstate-compatible index. The networking module provides deterministic /28 slice allocation per-tenant with optional NAT egress per-slice, tag-based route propagation, and explicit peering rules for cross-tenant control plane connectivity. State layout and migration: to avoid monolithic tfstate edits the PR adds a state-proxy migrator script that can split a large cluster state into three bounded statefiles (cluster-core, tenant-leases, tenant-network) and includes a dry-run mode plus idempotent checkpointing so we can roll back. Rollout plan: staged deploy using canary tenant leases, verify drain/reprovision flows in a dev cluster, run migrator dry-run, then migrate one tenant at a time with observability hooks. Backwards compatibility: new modules default to opt-in via top-level variables; existing private-installer manifests will continue to apply unchanged unless maintainers switch to lease-aware modules. Testing: unit terraform tests + integration test harness that simulates 50 concurrent lease requests and verifies no more than configured pool size are active, plus e2e on a pre-prod VPC. Migration notes: operators must run the included migrator and validate tenant-network CIDRs; the PR documents a safe rollback path that moves resources back to the original cluster-core statefile if a post-migration validation fails. See related Linear items ENG-8543 and INFRA-121 for product context.

review_conversation: Jared Thompson (review): Can you expand on how the lease index is coordinated to avoid split-brain if two operators run the migrator concurrently?

Maya Singh (author): The migrator uses a checkpoint file and an acquire/release lock in the cluster-core statefile via a small lock resource; the PR adds a retry-and-backoff loop and a manual override flag. I documented the sequence in the migration guide.

Evelyn Park (review): IAM roles look broad in the first commit. We should scope the ephemeral node role to only the actions required for node provisioning and tagging. Also prefer separate service account per-tenant in GCP plans.

Maya Singh (author): Updated iam policy and split service account creation per-tenant. Permissions are narrowed to actions: compute.instances.create, compute.instances.delete, compute.instances.setTags, and iam.serviceAccounts.actAs. See updated variables.tf for kubelet identity mapping.
Carlos Mendes (review): CI flake on integration harness observed timeouts when simulating 50 concurrent lease claims. Are timeouts adjustable?
Maya Singh (author): Increased harness timeouts and added exponential backoff on the test harness to reduce transient failures. CI re-run passed.
merge_outcome: merged via squash by Jared Thompson on 2026-02-24 (merge commit: 7f3a2c2)
release_notes: Add lease-aware GPU lifecycle Terraform module (opt-in) to provide tenant-scoped ephemeral GPU leases and safe drain/reprovision flows.
Add deterministic network segmentation module for per-tenant subnet slices and route policies.
Add state-proxy-migrator utility to split monolithic tfstate into bounded statefiles with dry-run and rollback support.
Migration guide and rollback checklist included in docs/private-installer/gpu-lease-migration.md.
notes_for_ops: Before switching production manifests to use the new modules run the migrator in dry-run mode and validate the checkpointed mappings. The migrator produces a mapping file that must be inspected; see docs/private-installer/gpu-lease-migration.md for the rollback procedure.
testing_summary: Integration test simulating 50 concurrent lease requests completed in CI with 0 over-allocations. E2E smoke on preprod verified node drain, ephemeral reprovision, and network slice isolation with tagged routes.
